Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery is a Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) cemetery located in the Somme department of northern France. Here are the key details about this cemetery:

## Location and Setting
- Located near the village of Beaumont-Hamel, about 9 km north of Albert in the Somme region
- Situated on the Somme battlefield, in an area that saw intense fighting during WWI
- Part of the preserved Beaumont-Hamel Newfoundland Memorial Park

## Historical Context
- The cemetery primarily contains casualties from the Battle of the Somme (1916), particularly from July-November 1916
- The area around Beaumont-Hamel was a heavily fortified German position at the start of the Battle of the Somme
- The village was eventually captured by British forces in November 1916 during the Battle of the Ancre

## Cemetery Details
- Contains approximately 100-200 burials (relatively small compared to other Somme cemeteries)
- Like most CWGC cemeteries, it features uniform white Portland limestone headstones
- Includes a Cross of Sacrifice, standard in CWGC cemeteries
- Some graves contain unknown soldiers, marked "Known Unto God"

## Significance
- Part of the larger Beaumont-Hamel memorial site, which is particularly significant to Newfoundland
- The nearby Newfoundland Memorial Park commemorates the devastating losses of the Newfoundland Regiment on July 1, 1916
- The cemetery serves as a permanent memorial to those who died fighting in this sector

The cemetery is open to visitors year-round and is maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission.
